cases.oracle: Fresh world with stone at (5,5): click 1 leaves the stone present with crack overlay stage 1 and cell damage hits=1; click 2 leaves it present with crack stage 2 and hits=2; click 3 removes the stone (cell empty), clears its damage entry, increments stone inventory by exactly 1, and the HUD shows the incremented count; wood behaves identically at hardness 3 while grass and dirt stay hardness 1 in the registry.

Fresh world with grass at (10,10): a single click removes the grass (cell empty), increments grass inventory by exactly 1, and leaves no persistent crack overlay or damage entry; dirt and leaf blocks are likewise removed on the first click (hardness 1).

With stone inventory >= 1, placing stone on an empty cell from the palette decrements stone inventory by exactly 1 and the cell becomes stone; with stone inventory exactly 0 a placement attempt is refused before any mutation: the cell stays empty, stone inventory stays 0, and the palette entry for that type renders greyed out at zero.

After mining and placing so that world cells and inventory both change, the saved blob at the single localStorage key is {version,cells,inventory} with per-type inventory as non-negative integers; a reload (fresh boot reading the same key) restores world cells and inventory deep-equal to the pre-reload state and the transient damage map resets to empty; with empty localStorage the first boot yields the default world and all-zero inventory.

cleanup.environment: Run from the repo root with the Node >= 18 built-in test runner; no browser, dev server or network access required; the run must leave no environment mutation.
cleanup.data: The logic suite injects an in-memory storage stub for the save key; no real browser localStorage, world blob or project file is written, and a completed run leaves no data artifacts.
